relationship: Selecting scheduling and interrupt decisions connects process states to the order and effects of a simulated workload.

learnerLoop.action: Choose the required decisions and step or run the workload.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Processes move through scheduler states as simulated time advances.
learnerLoop.evidence: The lanes, time badge, decision preview and comparison area show the outcome.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Revise a scheduling or interrupt choice to meet the challenge.

invariants: Process lanes and time evidence reflect the active scheduling run.
The simulated run applies the learner's ready-selection and interrupt decisions consistently.
safeAdaptations: Change workload stories, process names or guidance while preserving decision-led state transitions.

task.description: Three performance challenges and an unscored experiment, with live target evidence above the workspace.
task.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

rules.description: Drag or select matching amber Ready-selection and violet interruption rules into dashed empty gates; filled gates show the same rule icon.
rules.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

model.description: Amber Ready, violet Running and neutral Blocked lanes retain process identities. The decision preview shows the next dispatch and consequential interrupt comparison without repeating the whole queue.
model.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

evidence.description: State history, previous-run comparison, causal events and the recognised routine.
evidence.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

wait.description: Time a process spends Ready rather than Running or Blocked.
wait.domain: Integer ticks per process; mean Ready wait in the Convoy target.
wait.source: Selected rule pair applied to the workload.

response.description: Delay between arrival and first CPU service.
response.output: Response metrics and the Late Arrival/Interactive targets.

arrival.source: Arrival diamond drag or arrow keys.

modes.rules: Oldest Ready, shortest original job or least CPU left, paired with no interrupt, shorter-remaining pre-emption or a two-tick slice.
modes.challenges: Convoy mean wait ≤2.25; Editor response 0; Interactive maximum response ≤5; Experiment without a pass/fail target.
modes.support: No separate Working or exam toggle.

dependencies: Both rules are required to run.
Changing a rule during an unfinished run requires reset; previous completed evidence can be compared.
I/O blocking removes eligibility until completion, then returns the process to Ready.
implementation.completion: A finite workload completes when every process finishes; actual target metrics determine pass/fail and challenge checks.
limitations: One CPU, visible job estimates and no context-switch cost or priorities.
On narrow screens the timeline keeps all ticks and colour/hatching; fewer printed tick numbers avoid collisions.
